title: What is known about 1RB1LC_0RC0RB_1LD0LA_1LE---_1LF1RA_1LA1LC
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1LC_0RC0RB_1LD0LA_1LE---_1LF1RA_1LA1LC.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
The tape holds two binary counters, U up and V down. When V runs out the machine rebuilds V from the bottom digits of U; the rebuild is now computed exactly as a map on the counters.
verdict: The question is open. Lean proves the ticks; the exact macro map finds no halt in the first 10656 steps.
Where a halt would come from. Only from a rebuild after V reaches 0; which rebuilds halt is listed for small counters.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (D1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: The tick rules of the two counters
claims.text: For each of the headers 0110101, 0110111 the run uses, two theorems: with V odd, L 00000 (00001)^j 00 D>0110101 01 R becomes L 00001 (00000)^j 00 D>0110101 11 R in 10 * j + 38 steps; with V having i + 1 trailing zeros, L 00000 (00001)^j 00 D>0110101 (11)^(i+1) 01 R becomes L 00001 (00000)^j 00 D>0110101 (01)^(i+1) 11 R in 8 * i + 10 * j + 46 steps. That is U + 1 and V − 1 for every number j of carries and i + 1 of borrows and every tape L, R beyond (proved along the symbolic run of tools/py/bbtools/symtm.py).

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 178 cells have been visited and 50 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: The macro map and its simulator
claims.text: At each moment V reaches 0 the tape is the clean configuration 0^inf F U 00 D> H (11)^n 1 0^inf (F the counter's top word), so the state is (H, n, N) with N the up-counter read as one number. py/rebuild.py writes that tape, runs the rebuild (tick runs of its sub-phases jumped by the proved tick rules, the rest cell by cell in C) to the next clean tick configuration (H', n', N', V'), and then adds the V' ticks of the phase by arithmetic: next state (H', n', N' + V'), steps by the closed formula of the tick costs. Tested: its first 4 states and step counts, up to about 1054 steps, equal those of py/counters.py (itself tested against tools/c/tmrun.c).

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>656</sup> steps (macro run)
claims.text: The macro run from blank tape goes through 6 rebuilds without a halt; at the end V has 2,176 digits and the step count is about 10<sup>656</sup>.

claims.title: What the rebuild map looks like in the run
claims.text: Only 6 rebuilds fit in the 10-minute run (the seventh, with V of 2,176 digits, is run cell by cell and did not finish). Header and top word go round the cycle 0110111/1000, 0110111/1, 0110101/1000, 0110101/1. Every rebuild with top word 1 (3 of 3) left only a two-digit counter N' (2 or 3), so the next counter is 2n' + N' − δ, written almost entirely by the rebuild. The two with header 0110111 and top word 1000x kept the counter and V gained one digit; the one with 0110101/1000 read 33 digits. Six rebuilds are too few to call any of this a rule.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The macro map on (H, n, N) is computed exactly; its rebuilds have not been described for all N, so neither a non-halting invariant nor a halting run is known. The stopping walk found for 1RB1LC_0RC0RB_1LD0LA_1LE---_1LF0LA_1LA0LB (round 3) does not describe this machine's rebuilds: of the 584 rebuilds with N < 29 (both headers, n − len(N) + 1 in {0, 1}) on which the walk stops below the top digit, none gives the predicted (header, n', N'). No rebuild rule is proved in Lean for this machine (there is no lean/Rebuild.lean).

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Started on a blank tape, this Turing machine has run for 10<sup>9</sup> steps without stopping. This page runs the real machine in your browser, shows the shape of its run, and lists what is known, each result marked by what it rests on.

facts.text: No halt in the exact macro simulation (6 rebuilds).
Tick rules proved in Lean for every carry and borrow.

sections.heading: Two binary counters on one tape
html: Run the machine for a while and the tape sorts itself into two numbers written in binary. On the far left, after a single 1 that acts as a sentinel, is a counter U whose digits are blocks of 5 cells: 00000 is a 0 and 00001 a 1, most significant digit on the left. Then come a short gap 00, the head in state D, and a fixed header such as 0110101. Right of the header is a second counter V whose digits are pairs, least significant first: 01 is a 1 and 11 a 0.
The tick configuration is 1 U 00 D>0110101 V. Every tick adds 1 to U and takes 1 from V. Most of the time nothing else happens.

sections.heading: One tick: U + 1, V − 1
html: The head walks left through the trailing 1-digits of U, turning them into 0-digits (the carries), writes a 1-digit, then walks right to V and turns its trailing 0-pairs into 1-pairs and its lowest 1-pair into a 0-pair (the borrows). Written with j carries and i + 1 borrows:

beforeaftersteps
L 00000 (00001)^j 00 D>0110101 01 RL 00001 (00000)^j 00 D>0110101 11 R10 * j + 38
L 00000 (00001)^j 00 D>0110101 (11)^(i+1) 01 RL 00001 (00000)^j 00 D>0110101 (01)^(i+1) 11 R8 * i + 10 * j + 46

These two shapes are proved in Lean for every j and i (lean/Rules.lean), for every header the run has used (0110101, 0110111). Because the cost of a tick depends only on the numbers of carries and borrows, a long run of ticks has an exact cost: the sum of the trailing zeros of the numbers U+1, ..., U+k and V−k+1, ..., V, which has a closed form. The accelerated simulator uses it to skip billions of ticks at once.

sections.heading: The rebuild as a function of the counter
html: When V reaches 0 the tape is clean, 0^inf F U G S>H (11)^n 1 0^inf, and the machine's state is (H, n, N): header, length of V, and the up-counter read as one number together with its top word F. The rebuild then runs to the next clean tick configuration (H', n', N', V'), and the phase adds V' to the counter: the next state is (H', n', N' + V').

Here the counter's top word F is either 1 or 1000x. In the six rebuilds computed, those with top word 1 left only a two-digit counter N' (2 or 3), so the next counter, 2n' + N' − δ, is written almost entirely by the rebuild.

sections.heading: Halting, reduced to the rebuild map
html: Ticks never halt, so a halt can only come from a rebuild. The exhaustive runs of the rebuild for small counters list the ones that halt; whether the run from blank tape ever feeds one of them is the open question, now a question about the macro map on (H, n, N) rather than about the raw machine.

family: Up/down two counters with resets (G12 family 3b)
summary: Up/down counters with proved ticks; in the run every rebuild with top word 1 reads almost all of U; macro map on (H, n, N) computed exactly; no halt in ~10^656 steps.
